editions.text:
September 14 was the station's busiest day this week, recording 16 species and 232 feeder visits, a significant jump from the prior seven-day average. Regulars like Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees held steady on the tube feeders, while Northern Cardinals and Blue Jays maintained their consistent presence throughout the week.

This surge in activity follows the station's recent hardware updates. A new seed feeder installed on September 13 resolved detection issues, and the switch to a new microphone source on the same day ensured clear audio data. These changes align with the increased visit counts and reliable detections observed today.

The day ended with a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at sunset, capping a session where visual logs captured 11 species. While American Goldfinches and Eastern Screech-Owls were seen earlier in the week, they were absent today. The final hours brought quiet calls from Northern Cardinals and Carolina Wrens as the light faded.

The station woke to a steady drumroll of Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals before the light fully broke, with the first confirmed visual being a Tufted Titmouse at 7:08. By the time the sun cleared the horizon at 07:14, the feeder was already busy, dominated by a relentless presence of Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees. This early pace has held firm, with over 200 visits already logged by 10:30.

Activity is far heavier than the recent week, triple the average visit count for this time of day. The morning built from a quiet start with just a few calls in the 06:00 hour to a dense chorus by 08:00, when Carolina Wren detections peaked at 60 for the hour. American Crows and Blue Jays moved through the mid-morning, adding to the visual count alongside White-breasted Nuthatches.

A Black-capped Chickadee made its first confident appearance at this station this morning, a notable addition to the usual cast. Two Red-shouldered Hawks were detected, one in the early hours and another near the top of the hour range.

The afternoon holds the morning’s momentum, with 223 total visits far exceeding the recent average of 83 for this time of day. Tufted Titmice continue to dominate the visual records, accounting for 79 confident sightings, while Carolina Chickadees remain a steady presence with 64. The high of 28.7 C and light winds create a calm backdrop to the steady flow of birds on the feeder.

Carolina Wrens still lead the audio detections, though Northern Cardinals have surged in the recent hours, registering 19 detections at 14:00 and 24 by 15:00. The overall species count remains high at 19, significantly above the recent average of 11.6.

A single Gray Catbird was noted perched on a gravel surface, adding a rare visual to the day’s log.
